actions.name: Access Mediation
actions.description: Access mediation is the process of granting or denying specific requests to: 1) obtain and use information and related information processing services; and 2) enter specific physical facilities (e.g., Federal buildings, military establishments, border crossing entrances). Access mediation decisions should enforce least privilege by granting access for scoped durations to prevent privilege creep and, where applicable, implement just-in-time (JIT) access. Denial decisions may prevent initial access or terminate access that has already been granted, ensuring continuous enforcement of security policies.
actions.reason: Access Mediation directly establishes access granting by enforcing least privilege and scoped durations, aligning with the goal of controlled access.

actions.name: Network Access Mediation
actions.description: Network access mediation is the control method for authorizing access to a system by a user (or a process acting on behalf of a user) communicating through a network, including a local area network, a wide area network, and the Internet.
actions.reason: Network Access Mediation controls network-based access authorization, a critical component of establishing structured access granting.

actions.name: Access Policy Administration
actions.description: Access policy administration is the systematic process of defining, implementing, and managing access control policies that dictate user permissions to resources.
actions.reason: Access Policy Administration defines and manages access control policies, forming the foundation for an access granting process.

actions.name: Principle of least privilege
actions.description: Implement robust access control mechanisms, enforce the principle of least privilege, and regularly update and patch systems to close security gaps that could be exploited for privilege escalation.
actions.reason: Principle of least privilege directly supports access granting by limiting permissions to minimal required levels.

actions.name: Downstream Authorization

actions.reason: Downstream Authorization ensures access granting is validated across systems, maintaining security during resource interaction.

actions.name: Credential Revocation
actions.description: Deleting a set of credentials permanently to prevent them from being used to authenticate.
actions.reason: Credential revocation permanently deletes credentials, ensuring they cannot be used to authenticate and revoke access.

actions.reason: Account locking temporarily disables user accounts, directly revoking access to systems and resources.
